The IMF says liquidity, legal rules and settlement systems have not caught up. By Olivier Acuna | Edited by Sheldon Reback Oct 11, 2026, 9:00 a.m. EDT 3 min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on IMF headquarters Washington, D.C. (Henrik Gschwindt de Gyor/IMF) Summary Show Tokenized U.S. stocks offer round-the-clock trading and fractional ownership, with more than half of trades occurring outside regular market hours and about 80% involving less than one share, the IMF found. Overnight price moves carried useful information, with more than 85% reflected in conventional shares within five minutes of markets opening. The IMF said tokenized equities remain a small, fragmented market that could improve settlement and automation, but require stronger legal, liquidity and interoperability safeguards. Tokenized stocks
